description:
Intent i012 (SNAPSHOT=s03, branch=proc-config-write-unterminated) is complete. Artifact: agent-state/findings/i012.json (3 findings, 13 candidates, 6 limitations, snapshots_checked=["s03"]).

Finding 1 (medium): s03:arch/um/kernel/exitcode.c:46-52 - /proc/exitcode write (proc_create 0600 at line 70). size = min(count, sizeof(buf)) allows size == 7 on the 7-byte stack array buf[sizeof("nnnnn\0")]; copy_from_user(buf, buffer, 7) fills every byte with no terminator slot, then simple_strtol(buf, &end, 0) at line 50 reads buf[7] one byte past the array and the (*end != '\0') && !isspace(*end) check dereferences the OOB byte. Verified literal quote 'size = min(count, sizeof(buf));\n\tif (copy_from_user(buf, buffer, size))...tmp = simple_strtol(buf, &end, 0);...'. Untrusted source: write() count and contents; violated invariant: validated copy size equals array size with no +1 terminator; unsafe use: NUL-dependent parser past the array. Bounded to CONFIG_UML and a 0600 entry (seed-matching root-only trust boundary).

Finding 2 (medium): s03:drivers/scsi/imm.c:136-138 - imm_write_info, the ->write_info callback for /proc/scsi/imm/<host>. The untrusted source is proc_scsi_host_write (drivers/scsi/scsi_proc.c:64-87), which copies count (bounded only by PROC_BLOCK_SIZE = 3*1024 at scsi_proc.c:42) attacker bytes into a freshly __get_free_page'd PAGE_SIZE page with NO terminator write and hands raw (page, count) to ->write_info (scsi_proc.c:80-82). imm_write_info (read in full, lines 132-142) never terminates and runs simple_strtoul(buffer + 5, NULL, 0): with 'mode=' plus all-digit user bytes to the end of the validated length, the digit scan consumes uninitialized page-tail bytes beyond count and can run off the 4096-byte page (heap OOB read); the parsed value is stored to dev->mode. Fix primitive proven present in-tree: wd33c93_write_info terminates with buf[len] = '\0' (wd33c93.c:2019, in-bounds since len <= 3072 < PAGE_SIZE).

Finding 3 (medium): s03:drivers/scsi/ppa.c:137-143 - ppa_write_info, same proc_scsi_host_write untrusted source and same missing terminator; two simple_strtoul sites (buffer+5 'mode=', buffer+10 'recon_tmo=') scan past the validated count through the uninitialized page tail; the recon_tmo result is additionally emitted via printk (line 145), an unbounded-memory-to-log disclosure path.

Key safe counterevidence (candidates list): fs/configfs/file.c:195 fill_write_buffer writes page[copied] = 0, so all 53 CONFIGFS_ATTR files' sscanf/simple_strtoul stores receive terminated input; scsi_proc.c:424, scsi_devinfo.c:733, scsi_debug.c:6437, srm_env.c:107, xt_recent.c:599, acpi/proc.c:103, psi.c:1530 all enforce explicit termination or length-bounded parsing; cache.c:917/1521, svcauth_gss.c:1420, via-pmu.c:933, cifs_debug.c:1092, libipw debug_level, pktgen.c:534, pnpbios (binary), ntfs3 label (len-bounded nls conversion), sound/control.c:1598 (strnlen-bounded) were verified safe.

Limitations: proc writers using simple_write_to_buffer not individually audited; imm/ppa page-boundary overread is the worst case of the guaranteed beyond-validated-length consumption (no runtime PoC in read-only snapshot); powertec.c set_proc_info, aic7xxx seeprom writers, and sound/core/info.c per-entry write callbacks beyond control.c remain unclassified residue; debugfs variants in s03 belong to i010 and were not re-reported.
